newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Many W. Australia white lupin crops wiped out.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Many W. Australia white lupin crops wiped out.

text.p: The outbreak of anthracnose disease in Western Australia (WA) at the beginning of September wiped out many albus (white) lupin crops in that state, the New South Wales Farmers' Association general council meeting heard.

Gordon Frend of the association's oilseeds and pulses unit said on Thursday the crops were unlikely to produce anything as infected plants developed rotten patches at stem joints causing the branches to wilt to the ground.
"The effect is catastrophic for the albus lupin industry, although at 21,000 hectares (ha) it is less than three percent of the WA lupin area of 815,000 ha," he said.
"While other lupins can be infected, the effect is much less significant, but the outbreak may mean that the WA albus breeding programme is unlikely to survive," Frend said.

Xavier Martin, head of the association's grains committee, said affected properties in WA were being quarantined and systems put in train to quarantine movement from WA and other countries into New South Wales (NSW).
As with the sorghum ergot disease, the fungus disease could have entered Australia through breeders' seeds, he said.
The association is pressing Federal authorities for a strengthening of protocols for seed imports, he said.
Frend said there had been a drop of 25 percent to 106,000 ha of pulses sown in NSW this year because of an expansion of cereal plantings.
Lupins were responsible most of the fall and small reductions in chick peas, fababeans and field peas occurred, he said.
Most crops were in good condition with average or better yields expected, he said.
